title: FluencyCraft Advanced - Day 13
why_important: Handling crisis communications protects company reputation.

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): When talking about giving street directions (twice a week), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

options.a: Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.
options.b: I am giving street directions right now.
options.c: Signal crossing left turn take.
options.d: Signal crossing left turn take. yesterday

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'hedge against'?

options.a: Protect against potential financial or operational loss.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'hedge against' means: protect against potential financial or operational loss. Example: "We must diversify to hedge against market risk."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'drop by':

options.a: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'pick out':

options.a: Carefully choose specific items from a group.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'touch base'?

questions.explanation:

'touch base' means: briefly connect with someone to exchange news. Example: "I will touch base with you after the review."

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.
options.b: Your thought good but budget not allow.
options.c: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Telugu Scenario 3 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Word-by-word: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.b: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.c: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 4 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.
